children: By Phuong Nguyen and Mas Alina Arifin

Robusta coffee prices in Vietnam fell further this week on tepid trade on low stocks and soft demand after the country's long national holiday, while premiums for Indonesian robusta rose, traders said on Thursday.
Farmers in the Central Highlands, Vietnam's coffee belt, sold beans at 91,200 dong to 92,000 dong ($3.50 to $3.53) per kg, down from last week's 95,700 dong to 96,200 dong range.
"People have not come back from their holiday yet. Market is very quiet now," said a trader based in the coffee belt.
November robusta coffee futures settled down $14, at $3,392 per metric ton on Wednesday.
Another offered 89,500 dong per kg for coffee to be delivered in December.

"Although the USDA estimated that output in the current crop year would be similar to the previous one, many farmers said a large number of young cherries had fallen from the trees, raising concerns about production," the trader said.

Vietnam exported 1.33 million metric tons of coffee in the first eight months of 2026, up 13.7% from the same period a year earlier, government data showed. Coffee export revenue over the period fell by 8.6% to $6 billion. In August alone, the country exported 132,000 tons, up 13.7% annually.
In Indonesia, Sumatra robusta coffee beans were offered at $300 premium to the November contract this week, a trader said, up from $260 premium last week to the same period.
Another trader said beans were offered at $200 premium to the October contract, up from $175 premium last week for the September period.
Coffee farmers in Lampung said some developing coffee cherries had already begun to scorch.
